title: INSIGHT-Registry: A prospectIve, multi-ceNtre, SIngle-arm, real-world, post-market reGistry to assess the safety and effectiveness of Myval™ OCTAPRO+ TranscatHeter Heart Valve System in participants with sympTomatic severe native aortic valve stenosis
summary: This is a scientific study (registry) designed to collect data on standard clinical practice involving the MyVal Octapro+ aortic valve prosthesis. Patients scheduled for a procedure to treat aortic valve stenosis—a condition for which the MyVal Octapro+ aortic valve prosthesis (manufactured by Meril Lifesciences) is to be used—may be enrolled in the INSIGHT study. In previous studies, this valve prosthesis has proven to be safe and effective for the treatment of severe aortic valve stenosis; it is, therefore, clinically tested and approved. The INSIGHT study aims to gather additional information to gain a better understanding of how well the valve system performs in routine clinical use in Germany.

interventions.name: This post-market registry aims to gather insights from clinical practice (real-world data) regarding the performance and outcomes of the Myval™ OCTAPRO+ transcatheter heart valve system in German patients with symptomatic, severe native aortic valve stenosis.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	Consecutive patients who, in the judgment of the Heart Team/investigator, are suitable for treatment of symptomatic, severe native aortic valve stenosis using the Myval™ OCTAPRO+ transcatheter heart valve system
•	The patient has provided written informed consent for participation in the study prior to enrollment
•	The patient is willing to undergo all study procedures and follow-up requirements
Exclusion criteria:
•      Any illness or condition that, in the judgment of the investigator or the Heart Team, would preclude the patient’s safe participation in the study.
•	Patients with hypersensitivity or an allergy to aspirin, heparin, clopidogrel, ticlopidine, cobalt, nickel, chromium, molybdenum, or contrast agents.
•	Patients for whom antiplatelet therapy and/or anticoagulation is contraindicated.
•	Anatomical or clinical conditions that make transcatheter heart valve replacement (THVR) impossible.
•	Clinical situations that would preclude interventional cardiac procedures, such as active infective endocarditis or a similar infection.
•	Patients participating in another clinical trial for which the primary endpoint has not yet been reached.
